examples.input: `config set e "\n"` (the value is a single newline), then `config show`

results.1:
The arms on this route did different things. Two arms: exit 0; the file now reads:
e: |+

f: plain  # end
`config show` prints the same `e: |+` and a blank line. One arm: exit 0; the file now reads:
e: "\n"
f: plain  # end
`config show` prints `e: "\n"`. One arm: also exit 0 and writes the same quoted `e: "\n"` to the file, but `config show` prints `e: |+` and a blank line, so the file and show disagree. One arm: exit 3, stderr `troupe: write refused: e: cannot write this change faithfully`; the file is unchanged and show still prints `e: |` and `last`.
results.2:
exit 0; the file now reads:
e: |+

f: plain  # end
`config show` prints the same `e: |+` and a blank line.

context.in_practice: Both routes did the same for ordinary values. When the old marker couldn't fit the new value, both switched it: `|` became `|-`, and `|-` became `|+`. When it could fit, they kept it (`|+` stayed for c). They differ only on a value that is a single newline. Route 2 always writes it as `|+`. Route 1's arms split between `|+`, a quoted "\n", and refusing the write.
context.stakes: When a multi-line value is replaced, the `|`, `|-` or `|+` marker in front of it decides whether trailing newlines survive the next read. If the marker is wrong, the value quietly gains or loses newlines. A value that is just a single newline is the hard case: it can be written as `|+`, written in quotes, or refused.
context.tradeoff: Route 1 doesn't settle the single-newline case, so its arms ranged from a quoted value to a refusal (and in one arm the file and `config show` disagreed); route 2 always writes that value as `|+` plus a bare blank line, which is easy to misread or break when editing by hand.

plan_why: Changes block scalars so the chomping must change (| to |-, |- to |+), keeps |+ while its trailing blank line is replaced as part of the value, then sets a block value to a lone newline (|+ or refused); the final show checks every value reads back.
routes: Keep the old indicator if it can represent the value, otherwise choose strip/clip/keep from trailing newlines; keep-chomped trailing blank lines count as part of the value
Render a lone newline value as |+ instead of refusing it
